chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the one in Ihram who hunts birds.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the expiation for everything he attains.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِِمِ: The one in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for hunting birds while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of individual liability in Ihram violations, establishing that the expiation (kaffarah) is assessed per species caught rather than as a single lump sum. This ruling is central to Shia fiqh discussions on the precision of ritual penalties, distinguishing between the act of hunting and the specific type of prey. It underscores the meticulous nature of Shia legal methodology in applying Quranic injunctions to practical scenarios.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the one in Ihram hunting the birds.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him is the expiation regarding everything what he attains’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said
the following: “This is about a man who in the state of Ihram hunts a bird. He (the Imam) said, ‘He owes expiation for whatever he kills.’”
